_about: The test-links page (test-links.html) reads this list: Karl's change list. `checks` is the Features to check section at the top: one item per new feature (id, name, build, one link, numbered steps, what you should see), written from the real code and walked through with tests/features/walk.mjs before a build is called finished; the ticks live only in Karl's browser, and an item stays here until Karl has ticked it. The rest of the page: Live = on the site for everyone. Testing = behind a flag, waiting for Karl to keep or retire it. Retired = deleted. Every build adds or updates its entries (CLAUDE.md, Working with Karl). Each entry is a name, one plain sentence (`about`) and, for Live and Testing, its buttons. A button's `query` is the part after the address: card, level, seed, flags, sign-in skipped. `level` in a link is the saved level number (Add to both sides and Divide it: link level 2 is shown as Level 1). `reset: true` clears this browser's progress first; `look` is one sentence on what to look for; `notLive` says plainly why a link won't work on the live site.

checks.name: A nudge to combine, after Add
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click Add (the top button in the panel), type −4 and press Enter. The new row reads 3x = 19 − 4.
Move the pointer away from the panel and take your hands off for 5 seconds.
Press any key (Shift is fine).
checks.see: After about 2½ seconds the 19 and the −4 glow and pulse blue. A second or so later a small pop-up under them says “Drag one onto the other to combine them.” and a faint copy of the 19 glides onto the −4, again every few seconds. The key press clears it all at once.

checks.name: Work out a product: dividing first on Distribute
steps: Click the button. It opens Distribute, combine, solve, Level 1, on 3(x + 2) = 15.
Click Divide (÷), type 3 and press Enter. The new row reads x + 2 = (15) over 3.
Move the pointer away and take your hands off for 5 seconds.
Click the fraction bar under (15).
Type 5 and press Enter.
Click Add, type −2 and press Enter. Then type 3 in x =, press Enter, drag the 3 onto the x and press Enter for each line until Balanced.
checks.see: After about 2½ seconds the fraction bar glows, then a pop-up says “Click the fraction bar to divide 15 by 3.” with a ring closing in on the bar. Clicking it lights the (15) over 3 and opens a box under it: x + 2 = [ ]. With 5 the row reads x + 2 = 5. Add −2 writes x = 5 − 2 (nothing is worked out at x alone), and the check reads 3(3 + 2) = 15, 3(5) = 15, 15 = 15, then Balanced.

checks.name: Work out a product: a wrong product, and the × in multiplication form
steps: Click the button. It opens Distribute, combine, solve, Level 1, on 3(x + 2) = 15.
Click Multiply (the second button), then its second option (a box over a box). Type 1, then 3, and click the green Go. The new row reads x + 2 = ⅓ × (15).
Click the small × between ⅓ and (15). Type 45 and press Enter.
Press Undo.
Click the × again, type 5 and press Enter.
checks.see: A wrong 45 is lit with “check this” and “⅓ × 15 is not 45. Press Undo and try again.”; the ⅓ and the 15 stay lit, not greyed. After Undo a hint lights them: “⅓ × 15 is the same as 15 ÷ 3. Click the × and type it.” With 5 the row reads x + 2 = 5.

checks.name: The cross-off when dividing cancels the number in front of x
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click Add, type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the 19 onto the −4, type 15 and press Enter. The row reads 3x = 15.
Click Divide (÷), type 3 and press Enter. Watch the row (3x) over 3 for two seconds.
checks.see: In the row (3x) over 3 = (15) over 3, the 3 in front of x and the 3 under it are each struck through with a short red line drawn in, then fade a little; the 15 side is not struck. The next row reads x = (15) over 3, and the struck row stays in the stack until Next.

checks.name: The cross-off on a flip: the two minus signs
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 8.
Click Flip everything (the fourth button), then the green Go.
Watch the row −1 × (−x) = −1 × (8) for two seconds.
checks.see: On the x side the minus of −1 and the minus of −x are each struck through with a short red line; the other side is not struck. The next row reads x = −(8).

checks.name: Tab and the arrow keys between the distribute blanks
steps: Click the button. It opens Distribute, combine, solve, Level 1, on 3(x + 2) = 15.
Drag the 3 onto the parenthesis. Type 3, press Tab, type 6.
Press Shift and Tab together.
Type 4.
Press the right arrow key, then the left arrow key.
Type 3 and press Enter.
checks.see: Tab moves to the second blank. Shift+Tab goes back to the first and shows its 3 selected (white on blue); typing 4 replaces it (4, not 34). The arrows move between the two blanks the same way, each one selected as you land on it. Typing 3 replaces the 4 again, and Enter writes 3x + 6 = 15.

checks.name: The arrow keys between the top and bottom of a fraction
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click Multiply (the second button), then its second option (a box over a box). Type 1, then 4.
Press the left arrow key.
Press the right arrow key and type 5.
Click the green Go.
checks.see: After 1 the cursor jumps to the bottom. The left arrow goes back to the top and selects the 1 (white on blue); the right arrow selects the 4 in the bottom, and typing 5 replaces it. Go writes ⅕(5x) = ⅕(−15).

checks.name: Distribute: arcs the first time, labels only after a wrong product
steps: Click the button. It opens Distribute, combine, solve, Level 1, on 3(x + 2) = 15.
Drag the 3 onto the parenthesis and let go. Look at the equation and the two blanks.
Type 3, press Enter, type 5, press Enter.
Press Undo.
Drag the 3 onto the parenthesis again.
checks.see: The first time, the 3 turns blue, an arc with a small × runs from it to the x and another to the 2, “3 groups of” sits by the parenthesis, and the two blanks have no labels. The wrong 5 brings the labels “3 · x” and “3 · 2” above the blanks with “3 · 2 is not 5. Press Undo and try again.” After Undo the hint lights the 3 and the parenthesis, and the next drag shows the labels from the start (on this problem only: the next problem starts without them).

checks.name: A bare number for two x-terms gets a picture
steps: Click the button. It opens Distribute, combine, solve, Level 5, on 3(x + 2) + 2x = 41.
Drag the 3 onto the parenthesis. Type 3, Enter, 6, Enter.
Drag the 2x onto the 3x. Type 5 and press Enter.
Press x on the keyboard, then press Enter.
checks.see: A bare 5 brings a picture beside the two terms: three x boxes plus two x boxes, with the question “5 of what?” under them, and nothing changes yet. With 5x the row reads 5x + 6 = 41.

checks.name: Every check shows every step: Two-step equations, Level 5
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 5, on 4 − 3x = −11.
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter.
Drag the 5 onto the x.
Press Enter, and again, and again.
checks.see: The check writes 4 − 3x = −11 with 4 − 3 × 5 = −11 under it, then one line for each Enter: 4 − 15 = −11, then −11 = −11, then ✓ Balanced. (From Level 3 it used to jump straight to Balanced.)

checks.name: Every check shows every step: Distribute, Level 4
steps: Click the button. It opens Distribute, combine, solve, Level 4, on 5 − 2(x + 2) = −7.
Click the box after x =, type 4 and press Enter.
Drag the 4 onto the x.
Press Enter four times, slowly.
checks.see: The parenthesis is worked out where you can see it: 5 − 2(4 + 2) = −7, then 5 − 2(6) = −7, then 5 − 12 = −7, then −7 = −7, one line for each Enter, then ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Two x’s: one drop each
steps: Click the button. It opens Distribute, combine, solve, Level 5, on 3(x + 2) + 2x = 41.
Click the box after x =, type 7 and press Enter.
Pick up the 7 and hold it over the equation without letting go. Then drop it on the second x (the one in 2x).
Drag the 7 onto the first x (the one inside the parenthesis).
Press Enter five times, slowly.
checks.see: While you hold the 7, both x’s glow as places to drop it. The drop fills only the x in 2x: a small green check appears above it and a faint dashed 7 waits under the other x; nothing else happens yet. The second drop fills that x too, and the check begins: 3(7 + 2) + 2 × 7 = 41, then 3(9) + 2 × 7 = 41, 27 + 2 × 7 = 41, 27 + 14 = 41, 41 = 41, Balanced.

checks.name: Dividing by a negative: its own pop-up, once a level
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12.
Click Divide (÷), press the minus key, type 1 and click Go.
Press Undo.
Click Divide (÷), press the minus key, type 3 and click Go.
checks.see: Dividing by −1 is written as dividing, (−3x) over −1 = (12) over −1, with the minus signs and the 1 struck through, and a pop-up says “Dividing by −1 does the same thing as multiplying by −1: every sign flips.” (not the first-flip pop-up). Dividing by −3 then writes (−3x) over −3 = (12) over −3 with no pop-up: it shows once a level.

checks.name: Divide it: the whole number is explained again, and its / still works
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click Multiply (the second button), then its first option (a single box). Type 5 and click the green Go.
Click Multiply again, then the first option. Type 1, then press the / key, then type 5.
Click the green Go.
checks.see: The first option is not greyed. With 5 it says “5 × (5x) makes 25x: still not one x. Try dividing both sides.” and writes nothing. Typing 1 then / turns it into the fraction 1 over 5 (the 1 on top, the cursor underneath), and Go writes ⅕(5x) = ⅕(−15).

checks.name: Smaller numbers and One box sit beside Divide
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Look at the small dots to the right of each button in the panel.
Click Divide (÷), type 5 and press Enter.
Point at the two dots to the right of Divide, one at a time.
checks.see: Multiply has one dot beside it (No fractions); Divide has two. After dividing by 5, both of Divide’s dots turn green, and pointing at them shows “Smaller numbers” and “One box”.

checks.name: The Moves panel: its heading, the names and the symbols
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Look at the panel on the right.
Point at each button in the panel in turn, from the top, without clicking.
checks.see: The panel is headed MOVES in small grey capitals. Beside each button, on its left, is a bigger symbol: +, ×, ÷, a circle of two arrows, and a double arrow. Pointing shows each move’s property: “Addition property of equality: add the same number to both sides”, “Multiplication property of equality”, “Division property of equality”, “Multiplication property of equality: multiply both sides by −1”, “Symmetric property of equality: if a = b, then b = a”.

checks.name: Add no longer stays selected when you choose another move
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click Add (the top button in the panel). It turns yellow and a box opens under the equation. Type 4.
Click Multiply (the second button).
checks.see: After step 3 Add is white again and its box (with the 4) is gone from under the equation, as if Add had never been clicked. Only Multiply is yellow, with its two options beside it.

checks.name: A preview ends as soon as the pointer leaves Add
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Point at Add (the top button in the panel) without clicking. A grey row with two dashed boxes appears under the equation.
Move the pointer straight down onto Multiply (the second button).
Move the pointer off the panel, into the empty space left of it.
checks.see: At step 3 the grey row disappears the moment the pointer leaves Add; nothing faint is left while the pointer is on Multiply. At step 4 the equation stays clean.

checks.name: Pointing from one move to the next swaps the preview
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12.
Point at Divide (the third button, with ÷ beside it) without clicking. A bar appears under each side with a dashed box beneath it.
Move the pointer straight down onto Flip everything (the fourth button).
Move the pointer off the panel.
Click Divide. Then point at Flip everything again.
checks.see: Step 3 swaps the bars for the −1 × ( ) row at once; step 4 leaves a clean equation. After step 5 Divide stays yellow and keeps its own solid row (bars and boxes) while you point at Flip everything: a chosen move is not replaced by a preview.

checks.name: The Divide button: its preview, the row in division form, and the “same as” line
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Point at Divide (the third button in the panel, with ÷ beside it) without clicking.
Click Divide and type 5.
Click the green Go.
checks.see: Pointing shows (5x) over a long bar and (−15) over a long bar, each with a dashed box under it. Typing 5 puts 5 in both boxes and the line “Same as multiplying by ⅕.” appears under them. Go writes (5x) over 5 = (−15) over 5 with “Same as multiplying by ⅕.” under it, then x = (−15) over 5. Nothing is worked out for you.

checks.name: Dividing by −3: −3 under each bar
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12.
Click Divide (the third button, with ÷ beside it). Press the minus key, then type 3.
Click the green Go.
checks.see: Both boxes show −3 and the line says “Same as multiplying by −⅓.” Go writes (−3x) over −3 = (12) over −3, then x = (12) over −3, and nothing turns red.

checks.name: Dividing by −1 is Flip everything
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12.
Click Divide (÷). Press the minus key, type 1 and click Go.
Press Undo.
Click Flip everything (the fourth button), then the green Go.
checks.see: Dividing by −1 is written as dividing: (−3x) over −1 = (12) over −1, with the two minus signs and the 1 crossed off, “Same as multiplying by −1.” under it, then 3x = −12, and a pop-up: “Dividing by −1 does the same thing as multiplying by −1: every sign flips.” After Undo, the Flip button writes −1 × (−3x) = −1 × (12), then the same 3x = −12.

checks.name: The Multiply menu has two options again, and the fraction is back on Divide it
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click Multiply (the second button). Two options open beside it.
Click the first option (a single box). Type 5 and click the green Go.
Click Multiply again, then the second option (a box over a box). Type 1, then press the / key, then type 5.
Click the green Go.
checks.see: There are two options: a box ( ) = box ( ) and a box over a box ( ), with no small × or ÷ on them, neither greyed. The first, with 5, says “5 × (5x) makes 25x: still not one x. Try dividing both sides.” and writes nothing. The fraction takes 1 on top and 5 underneath on both sides, and Go writes ⅕(5x) = ⅕(−15), then x = ⅕(−15): written as multiplying, not dividing.

checks.name: The hint after Undo lights the Divide button
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click the box after x =, type 4 and press Enter. Drag the 4 onto the x, press Next twice and wait two seconds.
Press Undo.
Without clicking anything, type 5. Then click the green Go.
checks.see: After Undo the Divide button is lit, its preview (a bar under each side, a box beneath) is under 5x = −15, Multiply’s options stay closed, and the message reads “To get one x, divide both sides by 5 (that is, multiply by ⅕): one of the 5 x boxes is ⅕.” The 5 goes into both boxes, and Go writes (5x) over 5 = (−15) over 5.

checks.name: A fraction box can be retyped by tapping it
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click Multiply (the second button). Click the second option, the one with a box over a box. Type 1, then 5. A small note under the fraction says “Tap a box to retype it.”
Click the top box of the fraction.
Click the bottom box of the fraction.
checks.see: Clicking the top box empties it and puts the blinking cursor in it. Clicking the bottom box empties that one too, and the cursor moves there. The other box keeps its number until you click it.

checks.name: Type after a mistake: Divide it
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 3, on 3x = 6.
Click the box after x =, type 9 and press Enter. Drag the 9 onto the x, press Next twice and wait two seconds.
Press Undo. The hint says to divide both sides by 3 and lights the Divide button and shows its preview under the equation: a bar under each side with a box beneath it.
Without clicking anything, type 3.
Click the box with the 3 in it, press Backspace and type 3 again.
Click the green Go.
checks.see: After step 2 the check says the equation is not balanced. After step 4 the 3 is in the box under each bar, on both sides, and the line under them says “Same as multiplying by ⅓.” Clicking the box and typing again works the same way. Go writes (3x) over 3 = (6) over 3, then x = (6) over 3.

checks.name: Type on the problem after a right answer: Divide it
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 3, on 3x = 6.
Click the box after x =, type 2 and press Enter. Drag the 2 onto the x and press Next twice, then Next problem.
The next problem is 2x = 30, with “Your mental math is very strong.” Click Next.
Click Divide (the third button in the panel on the right, with ÷ beside it). Type 2.
Click the green Go.
checks.see: The 2 goes into the box under each bar, on both sides, with “Same as multiplying by ½.” Go writes (2x) over 2 = (30) over 2, then x = (30) over 2.

checks.name: Distribute, combine, solve · Level 1: a(x ± c) = b
steps: Click the button. It opens Distribute, combine, solve, Level 1, on 3(x + 2) = 15.
Drag the 3 onto the parenthesis. Type 3, press Enter, type 6, press Enter.
Click Add (the top box in the panel), type −6, press Enter.
Drag the 15 onto the −6, type 9, press Enter.
Click Divide (÷), type 3, press Enter.
Type 3 in x =, press Enter, drag the 3 onto the x, then press Enter until the check ends.
checks.see: The rows read 3x + 6 = 15, then 3x = 15 − 6, then 3x = 9, then x = (9) over 3. The check reads 3(3 + 2) = 15, then ✓ Balanced. The app never writes 3 for you.

checks.name: Distribute, combine, solve · Level 2: −a(x ± c) = b
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 2 on −2(x + 4) = −4.
Drag the −2 onto the parenthesis (no tap needed: −2 is the factor). Type −2, Enter, −8, Enter.
Click Add, type 8, press Enter. Drag the −4 onto the 8, type 4, press Enter.
Click Divide (÷), type −2, press Enter.
Type −2 in x =, press Enter, drag it onto the x, press Enter until the check ends.
checks.see: The rows read −2x + −8 = −4, then −2x = −4 + 8, then −2x = 4, then x = (4) over −2. The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Distribute, combine, solve · Level 3: n + a(x ± c) = b
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 3 on 5 + 2(x + 3) = 17.
Click Divide (÷).
Drag the 2 onto the parenthesis. Type 2, Enter, 6, Enter.
Drag the 5 onto the 6, type 11, press Enter.
Click Add, type −11, Enter. Drag the 17 onto the −11, type 6, Enter. Click Divide (÷), type 2, Enter.
Type 3 in x =, press Enter. Drag the 3 onto the x, then press Enter for each line until Balanced.
checks.see: Divide says “That move works once each side is one term.” The rows read 5 + 2x + 6 = 17, then 11 + 2x = 17, then 2x = 6, then x = (6) over 2. The check shows every step, one line for each press of Enter: 5 + 2(3 + 3) = 17, 5 + 2(6) = 17, 5 + 12 = 17, 17 = 17, then Balanced and “Yes! x = 3”.

checks.name: Distribute, combine, solve · Level 4: n − a(x ± c) = b
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 4 on 5 − 2(x + 2) = −7.
Click the minus in front of the 2. Then drag −2 onto the parenthesis. Type −2, Enter, −4, Enter.
Drag the 5 onto the −4, type 1, press Enter.
Click Add, type −1, Enter. Drag the −7 onto the −1, type −8, Enter.
Click Divide (÷), type −2, Enter. Type 4 in x =, press Enter. Drag the 4 onto the x, then press Enter for each line until Balanced.
checks.see: After the tap it reads 5 + −2(x + 2) = −7. The rows read 5 + −2x + −4 = −7, then 1 + −2x = −7, then −2x = −8, then x = (−8) over −2. The check shows every step, one line for each press of Enter: 5 − 2(4 + 2) = −7, 5 − 2(6) = −7, 5 − 12 = −7, −7 = −7, then Balanced and “Yes! x = 4”.

checks.name: Distribute, combine, solve · Level 5: like x-terms
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 5 on 3(x + 2) + 2x = 41.
Drag the 3 onto the parenthesis. Type 3, Enter, 6, Enter.
Drag the 2x onto the 3x, type 5x, press Enter.
Click Add, type −6, Enter. Drag the 41 onto the −6, type 35, Enter.
Click Divide (÷), type 5, Enter. Type 7 in x =, press Enter. Drag the 7 onto each x (one at a time), then press Enter for each line until Balanced.
checks.see: The rows read 3x + 6 + 2x = 41, then 5x + 6 = 41, then 5x = 35, then x = (35) over 5. The check shows every step, one line for each press of Enter: 3(7 + 2) + 2 × 7 = 41, 3(9) + 2 × 7 = 41, 27 + 2 × 7 = 41, 27 + 14 = 41, 41 = 41, then Balanced and “Yes! x = 7”.

checks.name: Drag the factor onto the parenthesis: the labels above the blanks
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 1 on 3(x + 2) = 15.
Drag the 3 a little way and let go anywhere that is not the parenthesis.
Now drag the 3 onto the parenthesis and let go.
Type 3, press Enter, type 6, press Enter.
checks.see: Let go elsewhere, the 3 goes back and nothing changes. On the parenthesis, the 3 turns blue, an arc with a small × runs from it to the x and another to the 2, and “3 groups of” sits by the parenthesis. Two blue boxes appear under the equation with no labels above them (an x printed after the first). Go writes 3x + 6 = 15, and the panel’s third small dot at the bottom (No parentheses) turns green.

checks.name: Tap the minus first, then distribute 5 − 2(x + 2)
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 4 on 5 − 2(x + 2) = −7.
Drag the 2 onto the parenthesis.
Click the minus in front of the 2.
Drag the −2 onto the parenthesis.
checks.see: The first drag is refused: “Tap the minus first, so −2 is a negative number.” After the tap the equation reads 5 + −2(x + 2) = −7, and then the drag opens the two blanks, with arcs from the −2 to each piece and “−2 groups of”, and no labels over the blanks.

checks.name: The wrong second product (the piece not multiplied)
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 1 on 3(x + 2) = 15.
Drag the 3 onto the parenthesis. Type 3, press Enter, type 2, press Enter.
Click Undo.
checks.see: The screen greys; the second box (2) and its label “3 · 2” stay lit, with “3 · 2 is not 2. Multiply this piece too. Press Undo and try again.” After Undo the equation is back, the 3 and the parenthesis are outlined, and the hint says “Drag the 3 onto the parenthesis to multiply it by each piece.”

checks.name: Divide first on 3(x + 2) = 15
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 1 on 3(x + 2) = 15.
Click Divide (÷), type 3, press Enter.
Click Add, type −2, press Enter.
Type 3 in x =, press Enter, drag the 3 onto the x, press Enter until the check ends.
checks.see: Dividing writes (3(x + 2)) over 3 = (15) over 3, then x + 2 = (15) over 3, with nothing red. Add writes x = (15) over 3 − 2. The check reads 3(3 + 2) = 15 and ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Combine x-terms (Level 5), including a bare number rejected
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 5 on 3(x + 2) + 2x = 41.
Drag the 3 onto the parenthesis. Type 3, Enter, 6, Enter.
Drag the 2x onto the 3x. Type 5 and press Enter.
Press x on the keyboard, then press Enter.
checks.see: Dropping 2x on 3x lights both with “Combine” over them and a box under them. A bare 5 brings a picture beside them: three x boxes plus two x boxes, and the question “5 of what?”; nothing changes yet. With 5x the row reads 5x + 6 = 41.

checks.name: The ghost hand after 2.5 seconds
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 1 on 3(x + 2) = 15.
Click I’m stuck.
Do nothing for 4 seconds.
checks.see: I’m stuck outlines the 3 and the parenthesis and says “Drag the 3 onto the parenthesis to multiply it by each piece.” After about 2.5 seconds a faint 3 travels from the 3 to the parenthesis, and keeps doing so until you act.

checks.name: Practice distributing first
steps: Click the button. It opens Distribute, combine, solve, Level 1.
Click “Practice distributing first” at the top right, beside the level dots. Click Skip tour if a tour starts.
Click ← Packs, then Solve it.
checks.see: It opens Build it’s card Distribute, then combine, at its first unfinished level (Level 1 for a fresh student). ← Packs goes to the home screen, where Solve it shows Distribute, combine, solve after Two-step equations; there is no button straight back to the card.

checks.name: Play it like a student: Distribute, combine, solve
steps: Click the button. It opens Level 3 on 5 + 2(x + 3) = 17.
Mistake 1: touch nothing for 11 seconds. Then click I’m stuck.
Mistake 2: drag the 2 onto the parenthesis and multiply only the first piece: type 2, Enter, 3, Enter. Then click Undo.
Drag the 2 onto the parenthesis again, type 2, Enter, 6, Enter.
Mistake 3: Divide too early: click Divide (÷).
Mistake 4: add the wrong number: click Add, type 5, press Enter. Then click Undo.
Mistake 5: a wrong sum: drag the 5 onto the 6, type 12, press Enter. Then click Undo.

Mistake 6, a mistake, Undo, then type in the blank: click the button at the top of this item again (it starts the same problem fresh). Drag the 2 onto the parenthesis, type 2, Enter, 6, Enter. Drag the 5 onto the 6, type 11 and press Enter. Click Add, type 11 and press Enter. Wait two seconds and press Undo. Without clicking anything, type −11 and press Enter, then click Next.
Wait 3 seconds and watch the nudge: the 17 and the −11 glow and pulse, then a small pop-up says “Drag one onto the other to combine them.” with a faint copy gliding from one to the other.
checks.see: I’m stuck flashes after 10 seconds, and then lights the 2 and the parenthesis (“Drag the 2 onto the parenthesis…”). The half-multiplied product is lit with “2 · 3 is not 3. Multiply this piece too.”; Undo brings the same hint back. Divide says “That move works once each side is one term.” Adding 5 is lit as “did not eliminate the term”. The wrong sum says “5 + 6 is not 12.”, and after Undo the 5 and the 6 are outlined with “5 and 6 are like terms. Drag one onto the other to combine them.” Mistake 6: after Undo the Add box is open again; the −11 you type goes straight into it, Enter writes 11 + 2x − 11 = 17 − 11, and Next writes 2x = 17 − 11. Waiting at 2x = 17 − 11 nudges the 17 and the −11.

checks.name: A student placed by the quiz before Build L now gets the new Two-step levels

link.label: Open as a device placed before Build L

steps: Click the button. It opens the home screen on a device whose Solve it placement quiz was finished before Build L, with both Two-step problems right.
Click Solve it.
Look at the Two-step equations card (scroll inside the card to see Levels 5 to 7).
checks.see: Two-step equations shows Levels 1 to 6 open (Level 7 locked), and none of them marked done. Before this build that device started the card at Level 1.

checks.name: The placement quiz never says “Start at Level −1”

link.label: Open the Solve it placement quiz

steps: Click the button. It opens the Solve it placement quiz, problem 1 of 10.
Click “I don’t know” ten times, until the results show.
Under One-step equations, click the green button.
checks.see: The One-step equations button says “Start at Level 1: ax = b” (it said “Start at Level −1: x + a = b” before). It opens One-step equations at Level 1.

checks.name: The hint after Undo says “divide both sides by 3”
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter. The row reads 3x = 15.
Click the box after x =, type 15 and press Enter. Drag the 15 onto the x, press Enter twice and wait two seconds: the check works out 3 × 15 = 15 to 45 = 15 and says it is not balanced.
Press Undo.
checks.see: After Undo, the Divide button is lit, its grey preview (a bar under each side, a box beneath) is under 3x = 15, and the message reads “To get one x, divide both sides by 3 (that is, multiply by ⅓): one of the 3 x boxes is ⅓.”

checks.name: The placement quiz opens the new Two-step card at the right level

link.label: Open the Solve it placement quiz

steps: Click the button. It opens the Solve it placement quiz (the diagnostic), problem 1 of 10.
Click “I don’t know” twice.
Problem 3 is 5x − 2 = 18: type 4 and click Next.
Problem 4 is 2 − 3x = −16: click “I don’t know”. Then click “I don’t know” six more times, until the results show.
Under Two-step equations, click the green button.
checks.see: The results list Two-step equations as “Getting there”, with 5x − 2 = 18 right, and the button says “Start at Level 4”. It opens the new Two-step equations card at Level 4 (4 + 3x = 19 style), and Levels 1 to 4 are open on the card.

checks.name: Add, combine, divide on 3x + 4 = 19
steps: Click the button. It opens the new Two-step equations card, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter. The 4s cross out and a new row reads 3x = 19 − 4.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter. The row reads 3x = 15.

Click Divide (the third button in the panel on the right, with ÷ beside it), type 3 and press Enter. The rows read (3x) over 3 = (15) over 3, with “Same as multiplying by ⅓.” under it, then x = (15) over 3.
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter. Drag the 5 onto the x in 3x + 4 = 19, then press Enter three times.
checks.see: After Add the right side stays 19 − 4 until you put it together: nothing is worked out for you. The check reads 3x + 4 = 19, then 3 × 5 + 4 = 19 under it, down to 19 = 19 and Balanced.

checks.name: Add at 3x = 15: the three x boxes message
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −3 and press Enter (trying to cancel the 3 in 3x).
Read the message, then click Undo.
checks.see: The 3x is outlined and the message says “3x is three x boxes, not a 3 to cancel. Adding −3 does not take them away. To get one x, divide both sides by 3 (that is, multiply by ⅓): one of the three x boxes is ⅓.” After Undo, the Divide button is lit and previewed, and the hint says “divide both sides by 3 (that is, multiply by ⅓): one of the 3 x boxes is ⅓”.

checks.name: Divide is greyed until each side is one term
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click Divide (the third button in the panel, with ÷ beside it; it is greyed).
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter twice (the second Enter is Next). Click Divide again.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter. Click Divide once more.
checks.see: The first two times it says “That move works once each side is one term.” and nothing opens. Once the row is 3x = 15, Divide is no longer greyed and its row opens under the equation: a bar under each side with a box beneath it, the cursor in the box.

checks.name: Level 3: Trade places first, with the symmetric-property line
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 3, on 19 = 4 + 3x.
Read the pop-up beside the panel and look at the Trade places box (the fourth one).
Click Trade places.
checks.see: The pop-up ends “This is the symmetric property: if a = b, then b = a.” and Trade places has a blue ring. After the click the new row reads 4 + 3x = 19.

checks.name: b − ax = c with Flip everything: 4 − 3x = −11
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 5, on 4 − 3x = −11.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the −11 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type −15 and press Enter. The row reads −3x = −15.
Click Flip everything (the third box in the panel), then the green Go.
Click Divide (the third button in the panel on the right, with ÷ beside it), type 3 and press Enter.
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter. Drag the 5 onto the x, then press Enter for each line until Balanced (every check shows every step).
checks.see: After the flip a pop-up says “Multiplying both sides by −1 flips every sign. −x becomes x.” and the row reads 3x = 15. The check starts 4 − 3x = −11, then one line for each Enter: 4 − 3 × 5 = −11, 4 − 15 = −11, −11 = −11, then Balanced.

checks.name: Flip everything: the first flip says what −1 does (once)
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Click Flip everything (the third box in the panel), then the green Go.
Click the box after x =, type −12 and press Enter. Drag the −12 onto the x, press Enter twice, then click Next problem.
On the next equation, click Flip everything, then Go.
checks.see: The first flip shows a small pop-up: “Multiplying both sides by −1 flips every sign. −x becomes x.” The flip on the second problem works the same way but shows no pop-up.

checks.name: Finished old Two-step levels already count on the new card

link.label: Open the old Two-step card · Level 1

steps: Click the button. It opens the old Two-step equations card (now off the home screen), Level 1. Click Skip tour if a tour starts.
Type 6 and press Enter, then press Enter again for the next problem. Do the same with 8, 1, 3 and 2.
Click ← Packs at the top left, then Solve it.
checks.see: The old card says Level 1 is complete. On the home screen the new Two-step equations card shows Level 1 done and Level 2 open. (On a student’s own device, any old Two-step level they finished shows the same way, on the level of the same kind.)

checks.name: Level 1 (ax + b = c): a right guess makes the next problem a move
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19.
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter. Drag the 5 onto the x, then press Enter three times.
Click Next problem.
checks.see: The first problem ends “Yes! x = 5, and it balances.” The second problem, 5x + 8 = 18, opens with “Your mental math is very strong. Let’s try solving this next problem using a move first.” and Add has a steady ring.

checks.name: Level 2 (ax − b = c): 3x − 4 = 11
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 2, on 3x − 4 = 11.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type 4 and press Enter.
Drag the −11 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter.
Click Divide (the third button in the panel on the right, with ÷ beside it), type 3 and press Enter.
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter. Drag the 5 onto the x, then press Enter three times.
checks.see: Adding 4 gives 3x = 11 + 4, then 3x = 15 and x = (15) over 3. The check reads 3 × 5 − 4 = 11 down to 11 = 11 and Balanced.

checks.name: Level 3 (x on the right): Add first is fine too
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 3, on 19 = 4 + 3x.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter (instead of Trade places).
Hover over the top dot beside Add in the panel.
checks.see: The new row reads 19 − 4 = 3x with no red message, and the dot opens to “Fewer terms” with a green tick.

checks.name: Level 4 (b + ax = c): 4 + 3x = 19, with the short check
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 4, on 4 + 3x = 19.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter.
Click Divide (the third button in the panel on the right, with ÷ beside it), type 3 and press Enter.
Click the box after x =, type 5 and press Enter. Drag the 5 onto the x, then press Enter for each line until Balanced (every check shows every step).
checks.see: Adding −4 gives 3x = 19 − 4 (the x term stays second until the 4s cancel). The check shows every step: 4 + 3 × 5 = 19, 4 + 15 = 19, 19 = 19, then Balanced.

checks.name: Level 5 (b − ax = c): I’m stuck gives a reminder only
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 5, on 4 − 3x = −11.
Click I’m stuck (bottom right).
Click I’m stuck again.
checks.see: Each time the 4 is outlined, the Add box is open under the equation, and the pop-up says “Look at the +4 next to x. What would we add to both sides to eliminate it? Type it in the box.” No balance, counters or Teach me.

checks.name: Level 6 (negative answers): 3x + 4 = −11
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 6, on 3x + 4 = −11.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the −11 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type −15 and press Enter.
Click Divide (the third button in the panel on the right, with ÷ beside it), type 3 and press Enter.
Click the box after x =, type −5 and press Enter. Drag the −5 onto the x, then press Enter for each line until Balanced (every check shows every step).
checks.see: The rows read 3x = −11 − 4, then 3x = −15 and x = (−15) over 3. The check reads 3 × (−5) + 4 = −11, −15 + 4 = −11, −11 = −11, then Balanced.

checks.name: Level 7 (all mixed): 19 = 4 − 3x, finished by dividing by −3
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 7, on 19 = 4 − 3x.
Click Trade places (the fourth box in the panel).
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −4 and press Enter.
Drag the 19 onto the 4 beside it. A box opens under them: type 15 and press Enter. The row reads −3x = 15.
Click Divide (the third button in the panel on the right, with ÷ beside it), type −3 (the minus key, then 3) and press Enter.
Click the box after x =, type −5 and press Enter. Drag the −5 onto the x, then press Enter for each line until Balanced (every check shows every step).
checks.see: Dividing by −3 finishes in one move: x = (15) over −3, and the line says “Same as multiplying by −⅓.” The check reads 19 = 4 − 3 × (−5), 19 = 4 + 15, 19 = 19, then Balanced.

checks.name: Play it like a student: Two-step
steps: Click the button. It opens Two-step equations, Level 1, on 3x + 4 = 19. You are going to play a student who gets things wrong.
Mistake 1, ignoring the screen: touch nothing for 10 seconds. A good response is a gentle flashing of I’m stuck, with nothing else changing.

Mistake 2, skipping the fraction: click the box after x =, type 15 and press Enter. Drag the 15 onto the x, press Enter three times and wait two seconds. A good response works out 3 × 15 + 4 = 19 to 49 = 19, says the equation is not balanced, and leaves only Undo. Press Undo: the hint outlines the 4 and asks what to add to both sides. Click Got it.

Mistake 3, a move that makes it worse: the Add box is still open under the equation, so type 4 and press Enter. A good response lights the 4 and the 4 that was added, says they did not eliminate the term, and leaves only Undo. Press Undo, then Got it.
Mistake 4, a move at the wrong moment: click Divide (÷, greyed). A good response is a small note, “That move works once each side is one term.”, and nothing locked.

Mistake 5, a wrong sum: the Add box is open again, so type −4 and press Enter. Drag the 19 onto the 4, type 23 and press Enter. A good response says “19 − 4 is not 23. Press Undo and try again.” with the two numbers still readable. Press Undo: the hint lights 19 and −4 and says to drag one onto the other.

Mistake 6, a mistake, Undo, then type in the blank: click the button at the top of this item again (it starts the same problem fresh). Click Add (the first box in the panel on the right), type 4 and press Enter. Wait two seconds and press Undo. Without clicking anything, type −4 and press Enter, then click Next.

Wait 3 seconds and watch the nudge: the 19 and the −4 glow and pulse, then a small pop-up under them says “Drag one onto the other to combine them.” and a faint 19 glides onto the −4. Putting two numbers together is a step with only one thing to do, so it is nudged; choosing a move never is.
checks.see: Every mistake gets a calm answer in the real numbers, Undo is the way out of each error, and the hint after Undo points at the next move. Nothing is ever worked out for you. Mistake 6: after Undo the Add box is open again; the −4 you type goes straight into it, Enter writes 3x + 4 − 4 = 19 − 4, and Next writes 3x = 19 − 4. Waiting at 3x = 19 − 4 nudges the 19 and the −4 (it never chooses a move for you).

checks.name: Level 1 (−x = b): only Flip everything is needed; the other moves say why not
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right).
Click Multiply (the second box). Two options open beside it: click the first one (a single box), then the second (a box over a box). Then click Divide (the third box, with ÷ beside it).
checks.see: Add says “That move unlocks on a later card.” In the Multiply options the first says the same and the fraction says “That move unlocks on a later level.”; Divide says “That move unlocks on a later level.” too. There is no −1 option: Flip everything is its own button in the panel.

checks.name: Level 2 (b = −x): flip first, and x stays on the right
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 2, on 12 = −x.
Click Got it if a pop-up is open, then click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and the green Go.
Type −12 and press Enter. Drag the −12 onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: The flip writes −1 × (12) = −1 × (−x), then −(12) = x, with x still on the right (that is fine). The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Level 3 (−ax = b): flip, then divide
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12.
Click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go. Then click the green Next.
Click Divide (the third button in the panel on the right, with ÷ beside it). Type 3 and click Go.
Type −4, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: After the flip the equation is 3x = −12 (No opposite box turns green). Dividing by 3 writes x = (−12) over 3, which is not worked out for you. The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Level 4 (all four forms): divide first, then the flip
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 4, on 12 = −3x.
Click Divide (the third button in the panel on the right, with ÷ beside it). Type 3 and click Go.
Click the green Next. Then click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go.
Type −4, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: Dividing by 3 first gives 4 = −x, with no red light (either order is fine). The flip then gives −(4) = x. The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Level 5 (bigger numbers)
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 5, on −3x = 36.
Click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go, then Next. Click Divide (÷), type 3 and click Go.
Type −12, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: 3x = −36, then x = (−36) over 3. The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: A helpful flip: −x = 12 becomes x = −(12)
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Point at the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) without clicking: a grey preview appears under the equation.
Click it, then click the green Go.
checks.see: The preview is −1 × (−x) = −1 × (12). After Go it is written in, then x = −(12): the 12 is not turned into −12 for you. No opposite box and Solved for x turn green.

checks.name: A flip that makes it worse: the spotlight, Undo, then the hint
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12.
Click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go, then the green Next. The equation is 3x = −12.
Click the Flip button and Go again, then wait two seconds.
Press Undo.
checks.see: −3x = 12 comes back with −3x framed in red (“x has a minus”) and “Flipping 3x = −12 made −3x = 12: now x has a minus. Press Undo.” Only Undo works. After Undo: “To get one x, divide both sides by 3 (that is, multiply by ⅓): one of the 3 x boxes is ⅓.” with the Divide button lit.

checks.name: −3x = 12 divided by −3 in one move is accepted
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12.
Click Divide (the third button in the panel on the right, with ÷ beside it). Type −3 (the minus key, then 3) and click Go.
Type −4, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: It writes (−3x) over −3 = (12) over −3, then x = (12) over −3, with No opposite box and Solved for x green and no red. The check ends ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: Typed 12 for −x = 12: the hint points at Flip everything
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Click the box after x =, type 12 and press Enter. Drag the 12 onto the x.
Press Next twice and wait two seconds. Press Undo.
checks.see: The check shows −(12) = 12, then −12 = 12, and says it is not balanced. After Undo: “−x = 12 means the opposite of x is 12, so x is not 12. Flip everything: multiply both sides by −1.” with the Flip button ringed and its preview under the equation.

checks.name: Trade places on 12 = −x, with the symmetric property
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 2, on 12 = −x.
Read the pop-up beside the panel.
Click Trade places (the bottom box in the panel). Then click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go.
Type −12, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: The pop-up says x is on the right, to click Trade places, and “This is the symmetric property: if a = b, then b = a.” Trading writes −x = 12; the flip gives x = −(12); the check ends ✓ Balanced. (Flipping first also works.)

checks.name: The check shows −(−12)
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Click the Flip button (the third box in the panel on the right, −x → x) and Go.
Type −12, press Enter and drag it onto the x.
Press Next twice.
checks.see: The check starts with −x = 12 and, under it, −(−12) = 12, the blue (−12) right under the blue x. Then 12 = 12 and ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: After a correct first guess, the next problem needs a move
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 1, on −x = 12.
Without making a move, type −12, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
Click Next problem.
checks.see: The next problem (−x = 3) opens with “Your mental math is very strong. Let’s try solving this next problem using a move first.”, the Flip button ringed, and x = greyed until a move is made.

checks.name: Play it like a student: Flip everything
steps: Click the button. It opens Flip everything, Level 3, on −3x = 12. You are going to play a student who gets things wrong.
Mistake 1, ignoring the screen: touch nothing for 10 seconds. A good response is a gentle flashing of I’m stuck, and nothing else changing.

Mistake 2, dropping the signs: click the box after x =, type 12 and press Enter. Drag it onto the x, press Next twice and wait two seconds. A good response shows −3 × 12 = 12 turn into −36 = 12, says it is not balanced, and leaves only Undo. Press Undo: the hint says the minus belongs to x and lights the Flip button. Press Got it.

Mistake 3, dividing by a number that does not split: click Divide (÷), type 2 and click Go. Wait two seconds. A good response says 3 boxes can’t make 2 equal groups and pulses Undo. Press Undo: the boxes, the counters and the fractions to choose from appear, ½ crossed off. Click ⅓.

Mistake 4, forgetting the sign at the end: the equation is now −x = 4. Type 4, press Enter, drag it onto the x, press Next twice and wait. Press Undo. A good response says −x = 4 means the opposite of x is 4, so x is not 4, and lights Flip everything.
Mistake 5, pressing I’m stuck again and again: press it twice. A good response repeats the reminder with the real numbers (this card has no pictures yet) and still leaves the move to you.

Mistake 6, a mistake, Undo, then type in the blank: click the button at the top of this item again (it starts the same problem fresh). Click the box after x =, type 12 and press Enter. Drag it onto the x, press Next twice and wait two seconds. Press Undo, then Got it. Click Divide (÷), click the box under the bar, press the minus key and type 3. Click Go.
Wait 3 seconds and watch the nudge: x is alone now, so a good response nudges nothing. The other side is yours to work out.
checks.see: Every mistake gets a short message built from the student’s own numbers, and there is always one clear thing to press next. Nothing gives the answer away. Mistake 6: the −3 goes into the box you clicked (under both bars), and Go writes (−3x) over −3 = (12) over −3. Waiting at the end nudges nothing: x is alone.

checks.name: Picking up your number slides a faint copy of the equation into the check

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click the box after x =, type −12 and press Enter.
Press and hold on the −12 and move it slowly toward the x, but do not let go yet.
Let go on an empty part of the page (not on the x).
Now drag the −12 onto the x in the equation and let go.
checks.see: While you hold the −12, a faint copy of x + 8 = −4 slides into the empty space on the right. Let go anywhere else and it slides back and nothing changes. Let go on the x and it stays there, solid, with (−12) + 8 = −4 written under it.

checks.name: The check writes the equation, then your number right under its x (Add to both sides)

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click the box after x =, type −12 and press Enter. Drag the −12 onto the x.
Look at the first two lines on the right.
Press Next twice.
checks.see: The first line is x + 8 = −4 with a blue x; right under it is (−12) + 8 = −4, and the blue (−12) sits directly under the blue x. Next adds −4 = −4, then ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: The check writes the equation, then your number right under its x (Divide it)
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click the box after x =, type −3 and press Enter. Drag the −3 onto the x.
Look at the first two lines on the right.
Press Next twice.
checks.see: The first line is 5x = −15 with a blue x; right under it is 5 × (−3) = −15, and the blue (−3) sits directly under the blue x (the first line moves a little to the right to make room). Next adds −15 = −15, then ✓ Balanced.

checks.name: At big numbers, a battle asks who won first; the subtraction appears only after

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 5

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 5, on x − 2 = −15.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type 2 and press Enter. The equation is now x = −15 + 2.
Click I’m stuck, then click Battle!. One small box appears just under −15 and +2: Who won? −15 or 2?
Click the big + first, then the big −.
Type −13 and press Enter.
checks.see: At first there is only the one box (no greyed second box). The + gets “Not that one”. After the −, a second box appears to the right: “Subtract 15 − 2 to find how many of the −15 are left.”, and the first box still shows the − you picked. −15 and 2 stay bright; nothing is written in x = for you.

checks.name: At big numbers, a party asks for its sign first, then what to add

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 5

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 5, on x + 13 = −2.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −13 and press Enter. The equation is now x = −2 − 13.
Click I’m stuck, then click Party!. One small box appears: A party of what? Pick the sign.
Click the big + first, then the big −.
Type −15 and press Enter.
checks.see: The + gets “Not that one. Look at the signs of −2 and −13.” After the −, a second box appears to the right: “Add 2 + 13 to find how many negatives.”, and the first box still shows the −. −2 and −13 stay bright; nothing is written in x = for you.

checks.name: A party of negatives typed without its sign gets a sign question

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 5

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 5, on x + 13 = −2.
Click Add, type −13 and press Enter. The equation is now x = −2 − 13.
Click the box after x =, type 15 (forgetting the sign) and press Enter. Drag the 15 onto the x, press Next twice and wait two seconds. Press Undo.
In the box at −2 and −13, click the big + first, then the big −.
Type −15, press Enter, drag it onto the x and press Next twice.
checks.see: After Undo, a box at the two numbers (both bright, the rest grey) says “−2 and −13 are both negatives. A party of negatives makes ___”. The + gets “Look again…” and the same question; the − says “Now type x, and keep the sign.” with x = bright. The −15 ends ✓ Balanced. (A wrong size, like −17, gets the usual hint instead.)

checks.name: A wrong sum keeps the two numbers lit

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type −8 and click Go. The equation is now x = −4 − 8.
Press and hold on the −4, drag it onto the −8 and let go. A box asks for their sum: type 5 and press Enter (a wrong sum on purpose).
Wait two seconds.
checks.see: The screen goes grey and a box says −4 − 8 is not 5, with Undo pulsing. The −4 and the −8 stay bright next to the box marked “check this”: they are what the question is about.

checks.name: A wrong answer keeps its reason lit, and your number is blue (Add to both sides)

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.

Click the top box in the panel on the right (+ ▢ = + ▢: that is Add). Type 5 and press Enter. The equation now has x alone: x = −3 + 5.

Click Battle!

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 1, on x + 8 = 11.
Press and hold on the +8 in the equation and drag it just to the left of the x. Do not let go.
Keep holding and drag it across the = onto the right side.
Drag it back to where it started and let go.

checks.name: Enter does the move, and never gives another clue

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 1

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 1, on x + 8 = 11.
Click I’m stuck once. A hint asks what to add to both sides, and a box is open for the number.
Type −8 and press Enter.
Press Enter again.
checks.see: The first Enter does the move: x + 8 − 8 = 11 − 8 appears, and x is alone. The second Enter does nothing. Before this change, Enter after I’m stuck gave the next clue and the second Enter wrote −8 over your own number.

checks.name: The counters at x = −3 + 5 no longer say “Nice drawing!”

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 2

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 2, on x + 5 = −3.
Click Add (the top box in the panel on the right), type 5 and press Enter. Click I’m stuck, then click I’m stuck again. The two numbers arrive as counters on the right.
Read the words under the counters.

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click I’m stuck twice. The seesaw opens on the right. Type −8 and click Go. Click Battle!, then Next, then Party!.
Type −12 and press Enter. The seesaw now shows the original equation, x + 8 = −4, with an empty x box. Drag the −12 onto that x box.
Press Next, then Next again.
checks.see: When the −12 lands, the x box becomes 12 minus counters in a blue box with a small x above it, beside 8 plus counters, and the other side has 4 minus counters, each line written below it. After the next press, the left side is 4 minus counters and the beam is level. The last words are ✓ Balanced, and the seesaw says Balanced too. A check done beside the equation (without I’m stuck) is drawn as before.

checks.name: On the seesaw, a number over 12 is one labelled box

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 5, on x − 2 = −15.
Click I’m stuck twice. Type 2 and click Go. Click Battle!, then Next. Click Battle! again for −15 and 2.
Type −13 and press Enter. Drag the −13 onto the x box on the seesaw.
Press Next, then Next again.
checks.see: The x box turns into one box that says −13, with a small x above it (not thirteen counters), beside 2 plus counters; the other side is one box that says −15. The last line is balanced, and the beam is level.

checks.name: Add never gives an answer of 0, 1 or −1

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 2

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 2, on x − 3 = −1.
Click the top box in the panel on the right (the one that looks like + ▢ = + ▢: that is Add). Type 3 and press Enter.
Type 2 and press Enter five times. The next problem comes up.
Do the other four problems the same way: work out the answer in your head, click Add, type the number that cancels the one beside x, press Enter, type the answer, press Enter five times.
checks.see: The five problems are x − 3 = −1, x − 4 = 6, x − 6 = −9, x − 2 = 5 and x − 5 = −7, and their answers (2, 10, −3, 7, −2) are never 0, 1 or −1. The first one used to be x − 4 = −3, whose answer is 1; the −1 in the first problem is on the right side of the equation, and that is fine.

checks.name: The seesaw opens beside the work, never over it

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 1

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 1, on x + 8 = 11.
Click I’m stuck once (a hint asks what to add), then click I’m stuck a second time. The seesaw appears, with “Build the equation” above it.
Look at the screen: the equation is at the top left, the seesaw is on the right, and x = with the green button sits below both.
Now make your window act like a shorter laptop: hold Ctrl and press + twice (Command and + on a Mac). That zooms to 125%. Look again at the same things. Press Ctrl and 0 (Command and 0) to go back.
checks.see: At both heights the seesaw sits in the space to the right of the equation. Nothing is covered, and x = and the green button are still on the screen without scrolling.

checks.name: Divide it: the hint after Undo names the idea with the real numbers
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15.
Click the box after x =, type 4 and press Enter.
Drag the 4 from the x = box onto the x in the equation.
Press Next twice. Wait two seconds: the screen greys and says the equation is not balanced.
Press Undo (bottom left).
checks.see: The Divide button (÷) is lit and its grey preview (a bar under each side, a box beneath) is under the equation, and the message reads “To get one x, divide both sides by 5 (that is, multiply by ⅕): one of the 5 x boxes is ⅕.” The green button says Got it.

checks.name: After a wrong move on the seesaw, the picture shows what cancelled and what did not

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4.
Click I’m stuck twice. The seesaw appears.
Type −3 (the minus key, then 3) and click the green Go.
It asks Party or Battle for 8 and −3. Click Battle!, then click the green Next.
It asks again, for −4 and −3. Click Party!
Wait two seconds.
Press Undo.
checks.see: After the wait the screen greys. On the seesaw the +8 and the −3 each show three pairs crossed off, with the 5 left over marked “still here”, the other side is lit, and the message reads “Battle! 8 and −3: 3 pairs cancel (crossed off), but 5 is still beside x. Press Undo.” Undo pulses with an arrow. After Undo, a hint points at the +8 and asks what to add.

checks.name: At x = −3 + 5: choose Party or Battle, cross off pairs, count, type x

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 2

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 2, on x − 5 = −3.
Click the top box in the panel on the right (Add). Type 5 and press Enter. The work now reads x = −3 + 5.
Click I’m stuck. It asks “−3 + 5: party or battle?” Click I’m stuck again. Counters appear on the right: three − under the −3 and five + under the 5, with Party! and Battle! under them. Click Battle!
Tap one − counter. It and one + counter get an orange line through them.
Tap an empty part inside the dotted box around the + counters (not on a counter). Every pair that can go is crossed off.
Count what is left, type it in x = (2) and press Enter.
checks.see: The crossed-off counters stay on the screen, with the lines through them, and two + counters are left. After you type 2 the check begins: “Let’s check that x = 2 is the solution.”

checks.name: Play it like a student: Add to both sides

link.label: Open Add to both sides · Level 3

steps: Click the button. It opens Add to both sides, Level 3, on x + 8 = −4. You are going to play a student who gets things wrong.
Mistake 1, ignoring the screen: touch nothing for 10 seconds. A good response is a gentle flashing of I’m stuck, with nothing else changing and nothing taken away.

Mistake 2, a wrong answer from the start: click the box after x =, type −4 (copying the number on the right) and press Enter. Drag the −4 onto the x in the equation. Press Next twice and wait two seconds. A good response writes x + 8 = −4 with (−4) + 8 = −4 under it, turns that into 4 = −4, says the equation is not balanced, and leaves only Undo to press. Press Undo, then Got it.

Mistake 3, a move that makes it worse: type 8 (the box under the equation is open) and click the green Go. Wait two seconds. A good response marks the 16 “got bigger”, explains with your own numbers (+8 + +8 did not eliminate the term), and pulses Undo. Press Undo, then Got it.

Mistake 4, a move that only half cancels: type −5 and click Go. Wait two seconds. A good response marks the leftover 3 “still here” and says +8 was only partially canceled by the −5 you added. Press Undo, then Got it.

Mistake 5, pressing I’m stuck again and again: press it four times. A good response gives a bigger clue each time (look at the +8, then which number cancels it, then choose Add, then “−8 cancels the +8. Add it to both sides yourself.”) and still leaves the move to you.

Mistake 6, a mistake, Undo, then type in the blank: click the button at the top of this item again (it starts the same problem fresh). Click Add (the first box in the panel on the right), type 8 and click the green Go. Wait two seconds and press Undo. Without clicking anything, type −8, then click Go.
Wait 3 seconds and watch the nudge: x is alone now, so a good response nudges nothing. Working out −4 − 8 and typing x is yours to do.
checks.see: Every mistake gets a short message built from the student’s own numbers, and there is always one clear thing to press next. Nobody is left stuck, and nothing gives the answer away. Mistake 6: after Undo the Add box under the equation is open again; the −8 you type goes straight into it, and Go writes x = −4 − 8. Waiting at the end nudges nothing: x is alone.

checks.name: Play it like a student: Divide it
steps: Click the button. It opens Divide it, Level 2, on 5x = −15. You are going to play a student who gets things wrong.
Mistake 1, ignoring the screen: touch nothing for 10 seconds. A good response is a gentle flashing of I’m stuck, with nothing else changing and nothing taken away.

Mistake 2, a wrong answer from the start: click the box after x =, type −15 (copying the number on the right) and press Enter. Drag the −15 onto the x. Press Next twice and wait two seconds. A good response writes 5x = −15 with 5 × (−15) = −15 under it, turns that into −75 = −15, says the equation is not balanced, and leaves only Undo to press. Press Undo, then Got it.

Mistake 3, a move that does not get one x: click Multiply, then its first option (a single box), type 5 and click Go. A good response says “5 × (5x) makes 25x: still not one x. Try dividing both sides.” in a small note, and writes nothing.
Mistake 4, flipping the sign: click Divide (÷), press the minus key, type 1 and click Go. A good response says the sign changes but there are still 5 x’s, and points to dividing.

Mistake 5, dividing by a number that does not split: click Divide (÷), type 2 and click Go. Wait two seconds. A good response says it doesn’t split (5 boxes can’t make 2 equal groups, and −15 can’t be shared into 2 equal groups), and pulses Undo. Press Undo: it shows the five x boxes and the fractions to choose from. Press Got it.
Mistake 6, pressing I’m stuck: press it twice. A good response gives a bigger clue the second time (first the 5 boxes and 15 counters, then “take ⅕ of both sides”) and still leaves the move to you.

Mistake 7, a mistake, Undo, then type in the blank: click the button at the top of this item again (it starts the same problem fresh). Click the box after x =, type 3 and press Enter. Drag the 3 onto the x, press Next twice and wait two seconds. Press Undo. Without clicking anything, type 5, then click the green Go.
Wait 3 seconds and watch the nudge: x is alone now, so a good response nudges nothing (and on 5x = −15, choosing the move is the thinking: only I’m stuck flashes, after 10 seconds).
checks.see: Every mistake gets a short message built from the student’s own numbers, and there is always one clear thing to press next. Nobody is left stuck, and nothing gives the answer away. Mistake 7: after Undo the hint lights the Divide button and shows its blank under each side; the 5 you type goes straight into it, on both sides, and Go writes (5x) over 5 = (−15) over 5. Waiting at the end nudges nothing: x is alone.

Flip everything (multiply both sides by −1) takes the minus off x; from Level 3 a fraction of both sides finishes, in either order or as −⅓ in one move. Trade places is live where x is on the right. Help is a reminder with the real numbers (no pictures yet). It sits after Divide it on the Solve it screen. "See why it works" is not built yet, so the card has no button for it.

items.name: Build I, Part 1: the check writes the equation, then your number under its x (2026-10-21)
items.about: When you check a value, the space on the right starts with the equation itself (every x blue) and, directly under it, the same equation with your number in place of x, the number right under the x it replaced. Picking the number up slides a faint copy of the equation in; a drop on x makes it solid, a drop anywhere else slides it back. Then Next works it out as before. On every Solve it card.

links.label: Add · check x = −12
links.look: Type −12, Enter, drag it onto x: x + 8 = −4, and under it (−12) + 8 = −4 with the (−12) under the x.

links.label: Divide it · check x = −3
links.look: Type −3, Enter, drag it onto x: 5x = −15, and under it 5 × (−3) = −15 with the (−3) under the x.

items.name: Build I, Part 2: big numbers, one question at a time (2026-10-21)
items.about: Past 12, after the right Party or Battle at x alone, one small box asks for the sign first (a battle: Who won?; a party: A party of what?) with a big + and −. Only once that is right does the second box appear beside it (what to subtract or add, worded with the sign), and the first box keeps showing the sign you picked. The boxes sit just under the numbers. You type x.

links.label: A battle at big numbers
links.look: Click Add, type 2, Enter, I’m stuck, Battle!, then −: “Subtract 15 − 2 to find how many of the −15 are left.” appears beside the first box.

links.label: A party at big numbers
links.look: Click Add, type −13, Enter, I’m stuck, Party!, then −: “Add 2 + 13 to find how many negatives.” appears beside the first box.

items.name: Build I, Part 3: a party of negatives keeps its sign (2026-10-21)
items.about: At x = −2 − 13, typing 15 (the right size, the wrong sign) is checked as usual and is not balanced; after Undo a box at the two numbers says “−2 and −13 are both negatives. A party of negatives makes ___” with a big + and −. The right pick says “Now type x, and keep the sign.” The class sheet records the slip as party-neg-sign, with the usual word hint.

links.label: x + 13 = −2, typed 15
links.look: Click Add, type −13, Enter; type 15, Enter, drag it onto x, Next twice, Undo: the sign question at −2 and −13.

items.name: Build H, Part 1: the quick fixes (2026-10-21)
items.about: Not balanced keeps its reason lit; the value you drop in is blue; each x already filled gets a small green check (for later cards with two x’s); the faint number starts after 2½ seconds; “Now type x” keeps the two numbers bright; a dragged term shows the same grey preview on both sides; a typed / turns Multiply into the fraction box; fraction boxes are retyped by tapping; Enter never gives another clue; and “Nice drawing!” is gone from the counters you did not draw. Each one is a Features to check item at the top of this page.

links.look: Type −4, Enter, drag it onto x, press Next twice: the last line 4 = −4 and “Not balanced” stay bright, the −4 in the first line is blue.

items.name: Build H, Part 2: the seesaw mirrors the check (2026-10-21)
items.about: When the seesaw was opened by I’m stuck or Teach me, checking an answer redraws the seesaw as the original equation and draws each line of the check on it: the x box becomes counters in a box with a small x above it (one labelled box past 12), and the last line is balanced. A check beside the equation, without I’m stuck, is unchanged.

links.look: I’m stuck twice, type −8, Go, Battle!, Next, Party!, type −12, Enter, drag the −12 onto the x box on the seesaw, then Next twice.

items.name: Build H, Part 3: big numbers at x alone (2026-10-21)
